defects.claim_says: Executive Order 11841 (held only as an American Presidency Project text, which I do not cite) adds a new section 306 for a Development Coordination Committee and does not mention section 305.
defects.source_says: The repository holds a Federal Register text of EO 11841: jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11841.txt (40 FR 8933, govinfo FR-1975-03-04 PDF, file sha256 01b1b804...; committed 2026-10-17 in dbeafb608). That text confirms that the order adds section 306 and does not mention section 305 or the Development Loan Committee. So the claim's conclusion stands, but its description of the evidence held and searched is false.

reasoning: The genuine claim corrects the planted dates. first_end.date and whole_order_end.date are now 1979-10-01, which matches EO 12163 section 1-905 and the claim's own reasons. I checked identity, the one-clause inventory, the hashes and quoted spans, the ending, the savings clause, the only held FR disposition note (Revoked by EO 12163), and the earlier-end tests, and all are correct. The held FR texts of the parent's amenders do not touch section 305. However, the research_rationale says EO 11841 is held only as an American Presidency Project text and therefore goes uncited. In fact the repository holds the Federal Register printing of EO 11841, so the claim misdescribes the evidence base and the search. Under the brief's rule that every fact in the reasons must be accurate and the searches honestly described, I reject. The cure is to cite jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11841.txt for the section 306 point. That text supports the same conclusion, so the outcome and the 1979-10-01 end would not change.
